Optimize a single-producer, single-consumer bounded FIFO queue.

Headline metric: `total_ops_per_sec` (maximize).

Preserve the required interface:
- Provide a native shared library named `./queue-candidate.so`.
- Export the evaluator's copying C ABI.
- Implement enqueue and dequeue for copied byte values using the capacity and
  value size supplied by the trusted runner.

The candidate may use any language or combination of languages. The queue must
remain linearizable, must not fabricate or duplicate items, and must respect
capacity. Maximize trusted end-to-end operation throughput for the SPSC
workload.

Start from the editable Rust implementation in `src/lib.rs`. It is an
intentionally naive correctness baseline, not part of the trusted evaluator.

# Queue Optimization Repository

This repository-shaped fixture contains a naive Rust bounded queue and three
VibeSys tasks under `.vibesys/tasks`: `spsc`, `mpsc`, and `mpmc`.

Run VibeSys from this directory and select one task. The coding agent works in
the repository root, while the selected task supplies its objective,
correctness gate, and benchmark.

The fixture is stored inside the VibeSys repository, so it cannot include its
own nested `.git` directory. Tests and run setup copy it to an isolated location
and initialize that copy as a standalone Git repository before optimization.

[package]
name = "queue-candidate"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.78"

[lib]
name = "queue_candidate"
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[profile.release]

# Roadmap

You (the Orchestrator) own this file end-to-end. Update it every round
*before* deciding the round's task. The framework names this file in
your next prompt but does not inject or parse its contents, so inspect it
with tools and format it however you find useful. Follow these conventions
so the structure stays legible:

- **Major** items: structural changes expected to move the headline
  performance metric meaningfully. Derive them from measured bottlenecks and
  the objective rather than from examples supplied by the framework. Usually
  1-3 rounds each.
- **Minor** items: bug fixes, polish, gates (correctness recoveries,
  tiny kernel swaps, accuracy bumps). Usually 1 round each.
- Use one of these four statuses, and note rounds spent on each
  in-progress item:
  - `todo` — not started.
  - `in_progress` — actively being worked on this round (or recent rounds).
  - `done` — implemented, profiler-verified, hitting (close to) predicted impact.
  - `parked` — implementation is buggy or incomplete, but you believe the
    *direction* is sound. Returnable to `in_progress` later. Use this when
    the metric isn't moving for an *implementation* reason rather than a
    workload reason.
  - `abandoned` — the *direction* itself doesn't fit this workload. Strict
    requirement (see below) before flipping to this state.
- For each item include a one-line *why* (predicted impact, what
  bottleneck it addresses).

If any Major item is `todo` or `in_progress`, this round's task should
serve it. Do NOT drop into Minor work while a Major sits unfinished
unless that Minor is genuinely blocking the Major (state the dependency
explicitly when you do).

## `parked` vs `abandoned` — get this distinction right

These two are not the same thing and the loop's behavior degrades if you
treat them as one bucket:

- **`parked`** is the right call when (a) you predicted the change would help,
  (b) the implementation satisfies correctness gates, but (c) the headline
  metric did not move because the intended path did not activate or the
  implementation is incomplete. The direction itself remains believable.

===SPSC README===
# Queue SPSC Task

This task targets a single-producer, single-consumer bounded FIFO queue.
Candidates implement the evaluator's copying C ABI and export it from
`./queue-candidate.so`.

The repository provides an editable `src/lib.rs` with an intentionally naive
Rust candidate using one mutex and `VecDeque`. Build it from the repository
root:

    make

VibeSys resolves the evaluator package during validation,
then runs it during optimization. The evaluator command is not a repository
executable.

The repository implementation is untrusted and may be replaced with any implementation that
exports the same ABI. `--use-reference` only self-tests the evaluator's internal
model; it is not the optimization starting point. The manifest benchmark uses
three repetitions and reports their median as `total_ops_per_sec`.

===SPSC OBJECTIVE===
Optimize a single-producer, single-consumer bounded FIFO queue.

Headline metric: `total_ops_per_sec` (maximize).

Preserve the required interface:
- Provide a native shared library named `./queue-candidate.so`.
- Export the evaluator's copying C ABI.
- Implement enqueue and dequeue for copied byte values using the capacity and
  value size supplied by the trusted runner.

The candidate may use any language or combination of languages. The queue must
remain linearizable, must not fabricate or duplicate items, and must respect
capacity. Maximize trusted end-to-end operation throughput for the SPSC
workload.

Start from the editable Rust implementation in `src/lib.rs`. It is an
intentionally naive correctness baseline, not part of the trusted evaluator.

===SPSC TOML===
version = 1

[agent]
domain = "generic"

[evaluator]
name = "vibesys-evaluator-queue"
version = "0.1.0"

[accuracy]
entrypoint = "vibesys-queue"
args = [
  "check", "--workspace", "${PROJECT_ROOT}",
  "--scenario", "spsc", "--operations", "32", "--trials", "100",
]
timeout_seconds = 120

[benchmark]
entrypoint = "vibesys-queue"
args = [
  "benchmark", "--workspace", "${PROJECT_ROOT}",
  "--scenario", "spsc", "--repetitions", "3",
]
timeout_seconds = 300
result_protocol = 2

# Queue Candidate Contract v1

This document is the normative interface between the evaluator and an untrusted
queue implementation. Candidate behavior is accepted only when it satisfies
this contract; evaluator implementation details are described separately in
[`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md).

## Required artifact

Candidates must provide a shared library named `queue-candidate.so` in the
workspace root. The library may be implemented in any language or combination
of languages that exports the C ABI declared in
`include/vibesys_queue_abi.h`.

The queue uses VibeSys's `inprocess` execution mode: the evaluator loads and
invokes the library directly inside an evaluator-owned Rust process. The
candidate does not implement a network service. Process isolation used between
trusted evaluator components is not part of the candidate interface.

The header is authoritative for symbol names, signatures, constants, and ABI
version. This document is authoritative for lifecycle, concurrency, ownership,
semantic, and error requirements.

The evaluator's Rust runner is the only component that loads the library. During
correctness checks it runs in a worker process controlled by the Go Porcupine
checker. During performance measurement it calls the same ABI directly from
native producer and consumer threads.

## Lifecycle

`vsq_abi_version` must return `VSQ_ABI_VERSION`. The runner calls
`vsq_queue_create` with an item capacity, a maximum value size, and the exact
producer and consumer counts for the scenario. Queue capacity is measured in
items, not bytes.

The runner creates one opaque producer handle per producer and one opaque
consumer handle per consumer before timing begins. Each handle is used by
exactly one native thread, while different handles are called concurrently
against the same queue. An implementation that does not need per-thread state
may use thin handles that only reference the queue.

The runner destroys all producer and consumer handles before destroying the
queue. It drains the queue before normal destruction.

## Operations and ownership

`vsq_try_enqueue` receives a byte pointer and length:

- `VSQ_OK` means the value was copied into the queue.
- `VSQ_FULL` means all item capacity was occupied or reserved and the call
  retained nothing.
- The input pointer is valid only for the duration of the call. The candidate
  must not retain or access it after returning.
- Length must not exceed the configured maximum value size.

`vsq_try_dequeue` receives caller-owned output storage:

- `VSQ_OK` means the complete oldest value was copied to `output` and
  `output_length` was set.
- `VSQ_EMPTY` means no published item was available. Output storage and
  `output_length` must remain unchanged.
- `VSQ_INVALID` means the output is null or too small for the oldest value. The
  value remains queued, and output storage and `output_length` remain unchanged.
- The candidate must not retain the output pointer after returning.
- A candidate must never write more than `output_capacity` bytes.

For valid enqueue inputs, only `VSQ_OK` and `VSQ_FULL` are normal results. For a
sufficient dequeue output, only `VSQ_OK` and `VSQ_EMPTY` are normal results.
`VSQ_INTERNAL_ERROR`, or `VSQ_INVALID` for otherwise valid arguments, fails
evaluation.

Operations are try-style: they do not wait for space to become free or for an
item to arrive. Successful operations preserve one global FIFO order and every
successfully enqueued item is returned exactly once.

SPSC and MPSC use an exact linearizable bounded-queue model. A successful
enqueue atomically appends an item, `VSQ_FULL` is legal only when the abstract
queue is at capacity, a successful dequeue atomically removes the oldest item,
and `VSQ_EMPTY` is legal only when the abstract queue is empty.

MPMC uses a reservation-aware bounded-queue model to match queues that acquire
capacity before copying and publishing an item. A successful enqueue has two
ordered internal events within its call interval:

1. reservation consumes one item of capacity;
2. publication makes the copied item visible at the FIFO tail.

`VSQ_FULL` is legal when published items plus unpublished reservations equal
capacity. `VSQ_EMPTY` is legal when no item has been published, even if an
enqueue currently holds a reservation. Consequently, a capacity-one MPMC
history may contain an in-flight enqueue that later returns `VSQ_OK`, an
overlapping enqueue that returns `VSQ_FULL`, and an intervening dequeue that
returns `VSQ_EMPTY`. Publication order defines the global FIFO order. Both
reservation and publication must occur within the successful enqueue call, so
a completed enqueue is visible to every later non-overlapping dequeue.

## Value-size guarantees

The evaluator selects a fixed `--value-size` for each run, currently bounded to
8 bytes through 1 MiB. Every measured value in a run has that size. Candidate
implementations must still honor any operation length up to the maximum passed
to `vsq_queue_create`.

The producer may overwrite its input immediately after enqueue returns, and
the consumer may overwrite its output immediately after dequeue returns. This
deliberately requires copying and makes allocation and byte movement part of
the measured implementation.

The correctness gate probes actual lengths 0, 1, 7, 8, 9, intermediate, and
maximum for 8-byte, 257-byte, and 1 MiB queue profiles. It also checks input
retention, undersized-output retry, concurrent short/full-buffer consumers, and
unchanged output on empty and invalid dequeues before running concurrent
Porcupine histories.

The evaluator may run multiple independent benchmark repetitions. Its
`total_ops_per_sec` field is the median repetition, and the JSON output includes
the individual `total_ops_per_sec_samples` values.

## Unsupported contracts

Version 1 does not support zero-copy ownership transfer, queue-managed producer
buffers, batched operations, or lossy queue semantics. A candidate must not
infer such behavior from implementation details. Any future contract with those
semantics requires a new version.

## Trust boundary

The Go correctness checker remains in a separate process from candidate native
code and owns expected payloads, call/return timestamps, histories, and the
Porcupine verdict. The measured Rust benchmark and candidate library share an
address space to avoid per-operation IPC and FFI transitions. Consequently,
performance scoring assumes cooperative native candidate code; Rust memory
safety does not isolate the runner from a hostile library.

For scored execution, the Go and Rust evaluators, this contract, and the ABI
header come from a trusted input snapshot.

cat > roadmap.md <<'EOF'
# Roadmap

Conventions per the framework template (Major/Minor, statuses `todo` /
`in_progress` / `done` / `parked` / `abandoned`, one-line why each).

## Workload facts that drive this roadmap

Established round 1 by reading the trusted evaluator
(`vibesys/_resources/evaluators/queue/`), not by measurement:

- Benchmark = SPSC, `--capacity 1024`, `--value-size 8`, 2s warmup + 10s
  measured, 3 repetitions, median reported.
- `total_ops_per_sec` counts **successful** enqueues + dequeues only.
  `VSQ_FULL` / `VSQ_EMPTY` attempts are counted in `attempts` and score zero,
  so spinning on a full/empty queue is pure waste, and the slower of the two
  threads sets the score.
- Consumer does strictly more per success than the producer (payload validate +
  two 5-multiply fingerprint mixes), so steady state should sit near-full with
  the producer absorbing `VSQ_FULL`.
- Correctness gate also exercises capacities 1024/1/2/3 and ABI profiles
  (1024, 8), (7, 257), (3, 1 MiB) — non-power-of-two capacities and 1 MiB
  values must work; max slab needed by the gate is ~4 MiB.
- Host is an Apple M4, `hw.cachelinesize = 128`, L1D 64 KiB. Padding must be
  128 B, and the hot slab should stay inside L1.

## Major

- **M1 — Lock-free SPSC ring over a preallocated slab** — `in_progress`
  (round 1). Baseline is `Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>`: one lock acquire/release,
  one `malloc`, and one `free` per item, plus pointer chasing. All three vanish
  in a single structural rewrite to atomic head/tail over a flat
  slot slab. Largest single expected move on the headline metric.
- **M2 — Cache-topology and index-traffic tuning** — folded into M1 this round
  (128 B padding of the two shared indices, producer/consumer-private cached
  opposite index so the fast path never loads the peer's line, slot layout
  chosen so the 1024x8 working set stays in L1). Zero extra risk on the same
  edit; broken out here so a later round can tune it independently.
- **M3 — Steady-state contention shaping on the FULL/EMPTY path** — `todo`.
  Once the ring lands, the producer is expected to hammer `VSQ_FULL`, and each
  fresh acquire-load of `head` invalidates the consumer's store line and slows
  the side that actually sets the score. A bounded `spin_loop()` hint before the
  fresh re-check is the lever. Contract-sensitive: try-style ops must not wait
  for space, so only a bounded hint is admissible, never a sleep or a retry
  loop. Batching the `head` publish is *not* admissible — it would make
  `VSQ_FULL` legal when the abstract queue is not at capacity.
- **M4 — Codegen and build flags** — folded into M1 this round (fat LTO,
  `codegen-units = 1`, `#[inline]` across the ffi.rs -> lib.rs boundary).
  Cheap; kept as a named item for later `target-cpu` work.
- **M5 — Hand-written C or asm hot path** — `todo`. Structural fallback if,
  after M1-M3, disassembly shows Rust codegen leaving per-op overhead that the
  measured rate cannot explain. Only worth opening if M1 lands well short of
  its forecast with activation confirmed.

## Minor

(none yet)

## Done

(none yet)

## Parked

(none yet)

## Abandoned

(none yet)
EOF

data.content: Roadmap written. Plan below.

args.hypothesis: The baseline spends nearly all per-operation time on work that the SPSC workload does not require: `Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>` in `src/lib.rs` costs one lock acquire/release, one `malloc`, and one `free` per item, plus a pointer dereference to reach the payload. Replacing it with a lock-free ring — two 128-byte-separated atomic indices over one preallocated slot slab, each side caching the peer index so the fast path never loads the peer's cache line — removes all three costs and leaves only an 8-byte copy plus one release store per operation, raising `total_ops_per_sec` by an order of magnitude.
args.title: Lock-free SPSC ring over preallocated slab
args.activation_evidence: 1) `otool -tV queue-candidate.so` for `_vsq_try_enqueue` and `_vsq_try_dequeue` shows no `bl` to `_pthread_mutex_lock`, `_malloc`, or `_free` on the success path. 2) `nm -gU queue-candidate.so` still lists all nine `vsq_*` symbols. 3) A local 1P/1C free-running harness (implementer-written, not the canonical benchmark) at capacity 1024 / value size 8 reports successful-op rate for the new build and for the committed baseline build, and the new build is at least 10x the baseline. Report all three, plus the raw local numbers.
args.falsification_criteria: Activation is confirmed (no lock/alloc calls on the hot path, exports intact) but the local 1P/1C harness shows under 2x the baseline successful-op rate. That would mean per-operation synchronization and allocation are not the binding cost and that cross-core coherence latency on the shared index lines already dominated the baseline, so this mechanism cannot carry the metric on this host. Also falsifying: the ring passes locally but the trusted correctness gate reports a linearizability, conservation, or ABI-status failure that is inherent to the design rather than to a fixable coding slip.
args.expected_effect: Baseline per item pair is roughly one uncontended-to-contended mutex round trip plus a malloc/free pair, order 100-250 ns; the ring's per item pair is an 8-byte copy, two release stores, and an amortized peer-index reload, order 5-25 ns. Forecast 10-40x on `total_ops_per_sec`. The upper end is unlikely to be reached because the score counts only successful operations and the consumer's per-success work in the trusted runner (payload validation plus two fingerprint mixes) becomes the new rate limit, so the realistic landing zone is 10-25x.
args.minimum_acceptance_criteria: Retain only if the trusted median `total_ops_per_sec` is at least 3x the baseline median with the correctness gate passing and no tradeoff axis configured (`pareto-frontier.md` records no objective axes, so throughput is the sole retention axis). The 3x floor sits far below the 10-40x forecast on purpose: the benchmark takes the median of three 10-second repetitions, so run-to-run noise is expected in the low single-digit percent, and a 3x result is unambiguously outside it while still leaving room for the consumer-side rate limit to cap the gain well short of the forecast. Below 3x with activation confirmed, treat the mechanism as underperforming and park it rather than retaining an unexplained partial win. Accept no correctness regression and no increase in resident memory beyond the slab itself.
args.invariants:
Authoritative and unchanged: the ABI in `include/vibesys_queue_abi.h` and the lifecycle, ownership, and semantic rules in `CANDIDATE_CONTRACT.md` (both inside the resolved `vibesys-evaluator-queue` package; the local mirror of the exported surface is `src/ffi.rs`). Do not change exported symbol names, signatures, or `ABI_VERSION`. The build contract in `Makefile` — `cargo build --release --locked` producing `./queue-candidate.so` — must keep working unchanged.

Hypothesis-specific constraints, all derived from the contract and the evaluator source:

- Operations are try-style. `vsq_try_enqueue` and `vsq_try_dequeue` must never block, sleep, or loop waiting for the peer.
- `VSQ_FULL` may be returned only when the queue is genuinely at capacity, and `VSQ_EMPTY` only when it is genuinely empty, both judged at a point inside the call. A cached peer index may drive the fast path, but before returning FULL or EMPTY the code must re-load the peer's atomic index and re-check. Publishing the consumer's head lazily or in batches is forbidden: it would make FULL legal while the abstract queue has room.
- `VSQ_EMPTY` and `VSQ_INVALID` from dequeue must leave both the output buffer and `*output_length` untouched, and must leave the value queued. Read the stored length and compare it against `output_capacity` before copying any bytes.
- Never write more than `output_capacity` bytes. Never retain the caller's input or output pointer past the call.
- For valid arguments, only OK/FULL and OK/EMPTY are acceptable; any `VSQ_INVALID` or `VSQ_INTERNAL_ERROR` on a valid call fails evaluation. Keep the existing rejection of out-of-range producer/consumer ids.
- The crate is `panic = "abort"`: a panic kills the trusted runner. Slab allocation must be fallible and return `STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR` on failure, and the hot path must not use anything that can panic (no bounds-checked indexing on the hot path, no unwrap).
- Correctness must hold for non-power-of-two capacities. The gate runs capacities 1024, 1, 2, and 3, and ABI profiles (1024, 8), (7, 257), (3, 1 MiB). Whatever wrap scheme is chosen must be exercised at those shapes. Actual value lengths 0, 1, 7, 8, 9, intermediate, and maximum are all probed, so length must be stored per slot, not assumed constant.
- Host is Apple M4 arm64: `hw.cachelinesize` is 128, so shared-index padding is 128 bytes, not 64. L1D is 64 KiB, so keep the 1024-slot benchmark slab well inside it.
args.task:
Replace the queue core in `src/lib.rs` with a lock-free SPSC ring. `src/ffi.rs` should need no signature changes; keep it as the thin ABI shim and mark the shim plus the core operations `#[inline]`.

Component and interface:

- `QueueState` owns one fallibly-allocated slab of `slots` fixed-stride slots plus two shared indices. Each slot holds its own length header and its payload contiguously (for example a `u64` length followed by `max_value_size` payload bytes, stride rounded up for alignment) so one operation touches one cache line at value size 8. A parallel length array is the weaker alternative because it doubles the lines touched per operation.
- Producer index `tail` and consumer index `head` are monotonic `AtomicU64` counters, each alone on its own 128-byte-aligned, 128-byte-padded region so neither side's store invalidates the other's line. Monotonic counters make full and empty unambiguous without a spare slot.
- Suggested wrap scheme, since capacity 3 and 7 must work and a `%` on the hot path is a division: allocate `slots = next_power_of_two(capacity)` and index with a mask, while enforcing the logical bound with `tail - head == capacity`. Over-allocation is at most 2x, and the gate's worst case (capacity 3, 1 MiB values) is 4 slots and 4 MiB. Any equivalent division-free scheme is fine; state which you chose.
- `Producer` and `Consumer` handles carry their own private cached copy of the peer index. Enqueue fast path: compare `tail` against the cached `head`; only when it reports full, acquire-load the real `head` into the cache and re-check; return `VSQ_FULL` only if it is still full. Dequeue is the mirror image against `tail`. Handles are per-thread by contract, so this private state needs no synchronization, but pad/align the handle allocations so two handles cannot share a line.
- Ordering: write the length header and payload, then `Release`-store the advanced `tail`. Consumer `Acquire`-loads `tail`, reads header and payload, then `Release`-stores the advanced `head`. Each side loads its own index `Relaxed`.
- Add a small-length fast path in both directions: at length 8 do a single unaligned `u64` copy instead of calling `memcpy`, falling back to `copy_nonoverlapping` otherwise. At value size 8 this removes a libc call from every operation.
- In `Cargo.toml`, add `lto = "fat"`, `codegen-units = 1`, and `opt-level = 3` to `[profile.release]`, keeping `panic = "abort"`. Do not touch `Cargo.lock`; profile changes do not invalidate `--locked`.
- Keep the existing `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests passing and extend them to cover capacity 1, capacity 3, zero-length values, maximum-length values, undersized-output retry, and wraparound across more than `capacity` items.

Staged evaluation, cheapest first, stopping as soon as a stage fails:

1. `cargo test --release` for the extended unit tests, and `make` to confirm `./queue-candidate.so` is produced.
2. Activation checks as listed in the activation evidence field: the `otool` disassembly check, `nm -gU`, and the local 1P/1C harness comparing the new build against the committed baseline build.
3. Only if 1 and 2 pass, hand off. Do not re-run the framework's canonical benchmark; it runs after review.

Verification strategy — the minimum that exercises the failure-prone paths, which here are the wrap arithmetic, the FULL/EMPTY boundary, and the ordering:

- Single-threaded boundary test at capacity 1, 2, 3, and 7: fill to exactly capacity, assert the next enqueue is FULL, drain to empty, assert the next dequeue is EMPTY, and repeat across at least three wraps so the mask/wrap path is exercised past the slab end.
- Mixed-length test at max_value_size 257 and at 1 MiB with capacity 3: enqueue lengths 0, 1, 7, 8, 9, and max, dequeue them, and assert both bytes and returned lengths match FIFO order.
- Undersized-output test: enqueue a value, dequeue into a buffer one byte too small, assert `VSQ_INVALID`, assert the output buffer and the length out-parameter are byte-for-byte unchanged, then dequeue into an adequate buffer and assert the value is intact.
- Two-thread stress in the local harness: run producer and consumer for a few seconds at capacity 1024 with a per-item sequence number, assert every dequeued value is the next expected sequence number with no gaps and no repeats, and assert enqueued minus dequeued equals what the final drain returns. This is the cheapest check that would catch a missing Acquire or Release.
- Run the two-thread stress under a debug build too; the release build can hide an ordering bug behind timing.

If any stage fails, isolate along the changed dataflow — slot addressing, then length handling, then index ordering — before rebuilding and re-measuring; do not fix only the leaf assertion that tripped.
args.pass_criteria:
1. Activation: the `otool -tV` disassembly of `_vsq_try_enqueue` and `_vsq_try_dequeue` shows no branch to `_pthread_mutex_lock`, `_malloc`, or `_free`; `nm -gU queue-candidate.so` lists all nine `vsq_*` symbols; the local 1P/1C harness reports at least 10x the committed baseline's successful-op rate. Raw numbers reported, not just a verdict.
2. Correctness: `cargo test --release` and `cargo test` (debug) both pass, including the extended capacity-1/2/3/7, zero-length, max-length, undersized-output, and multi-wrap cases, plus the two-thread sequence-conservation stress in both profiles.
3. Contract: no exported symbol name or signature changed, `ABI_VERSION` still 1, no blocking, sleeping, or retry loop anywhere in enqueue or dequeue, FULL and EMPTY each preceded by a fresh atomic re-load of the peer index, dequeue leaving output and `*output_length` untouched on EMPTY and INVALID, and no panicking construct on the hot path.
4. Build: `make` succeeds from clean via `cargo build --release --locked`, `Cargo.lock` unmodified, `./queue-candidate.so` present.
5. Cleanup: no leftover scratch binaries, profiling shims, debug printing, or dead mutex/VecDeque code; the local harness, if committed, lives outside the hot library path and does not affect the cdylib build.
6. Evidence: report the local before/after ops-per-second numbers, the chosen wrap scheme, the slot layout and stride, and the padding size actually used.
args.reasoning: The run configures a single round, so this round must carry the largest available structural move rather than stage a search. Reading the trusted evaluator settles the parent and mechanism without measurement: the benchmark is 1P/1C at capacity 1024 with 8-byte values, and the score counts only successful operations, so the winning design is the one with the cheapest successful operation. The baseline pays a mutex round trip plus a malloc/free pair per item for a workload with exactly one producer and one consumer and a fixed maximum value size — every one of those costs is removable by the same edit, which is why the ring dominates any partial alternative. Rejected: a profiler pass first, since a `macos_cpu` sample would attribute time to `pthread_mutex_lock` and `malloc` inside code this change deletes wholesale, confirming rather than reranking; lock-free-with-per-item-allocation, which keeps the allocator on the hot path for no benefit at fixed value size; a spare-slot ring instead of monotonic counters, which complicates the exact full/empty predicate the linearizability gate checks; and batching the consumer's head publish, which is a genuine throughput lever but would make `VSQ_FULL` legal while the queue has room and so violates the contract's exact bounded-queue model. The FULL-path backoff idea is real — the consumer is the slower side and the producer's re-reads will invalidate its store line — but it is contract-sensitive and only measurable once the ring exists, so it stays as roadmap M3 rather than contaminating this round's falsifier. Cache-line padding at 128 bytes and the codegen flags are folded in because they are the same edit at near-zero risk on this host.

Component and interface:

- `QueueState` owns one fallibly-allocated slab of `slots` fixed-stride slots plus two shared indices. Each slot holds its own length header and its payload contiguously (for example a `u64` length followed by `max_value_size` payload bytes, stride rounded up for alignment) so one operation touches one cache line at value size 8. A parallel length array is the weaker alternative because it doubles the lines touched per operation.
- Producer index `tail` and consumer index `head` are monotonic `AtomicU64` counters, each alone on its own 128-byte-aligned, 128-byte-padded region so neither side's store invalidates the other's line. Monotonic counters make full and empty unambiguous without a spare slot.
- Suggested wrap scheme, since capacity 3 and 7 must work and a `%` on the hot path is a division: allocate `slots = next_power_of_two(capacity)` and index with a mask, while enforcing the logical bound with `tail - head == capacity`. # Progress

## Round 1 — Orchestrator (pre-round)
- **need_profile**: False
- **profile_focus**: 
- **reasoning**: Cheap check confirms the candidate builds and runs (run-init dylib exports all 9 vsq_* symbols; dlopen probe returned abi=1 and STATUS_OK for queue/producer/consumer create), so a profile is technically possible — my own cargo EPERM was a shell TMPDIR restriction, not a workspace defect. But static evidence already determines round 1's plan: the baseline is Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>> with a per-enqueue heap allocation and per-dequeue free, stacking mutex contention, allocator traffic, and pointer indirection on an SPSC path, and all three are removed by the same single structural rewrite to a preallocated cache-line-padded lock-free ring over a flat capacity*max_value_size slab. A macos_cpu sample would show time in pthread_mutex_lock and malloc, confirming rather than reranking the hypothesis, and would attribute cost in code the first Major deletes wholesale. The profile with real discriminating power (false sharing vs payload memcpy vs atomic ordering) is round 2, against the ring implementation.

## Round 1 — Orchestrator (plan)
- **hypothesis_id**: h1-spsc-lockfree-ring
- **reasoning**: The run configures a single round, so this round must carry the largest available structural move rather than stage a search. Reading the trusted evaluator settles the parent and mechanism without measurement: the benchmark is 1P/1C at capacity 1024 with 8-byte values, and the score counts only successful operations, so the winning design is the one with the cheapest successful operation. The baseline pays a mutex round trip plus a malloc/free pair per item for a workload with exactly one producer and one consumer and a fixed maximum value size — every one of those costs is removable by the same edit, which is why the ring dominates any partial alternative. Rejected: a profiler pass first, since a `macos_cpu` sample would attribute time to `pthread_mutex_lock` and `malloc` inside code this change deletes wholesale, confirming rather than reranking; lock-free-with-per-item-allocation, which keeps the allocator on the hot path for no benefit at fixed value size; a spare-slot ring instead of monotonic counters, which complicates the exact full/empty predicate the linearizability gate checks; and batching the consumer's head publish, which is a genuine throughput lever but would make `VSQ_FULL` legal while the queue has room and so violates the contract's exact bounded-queue model. The FULL-path backoff idea is real — the consumer is the slower side and the producer's re-reads will invalidate its store line — but it is contract-sensitive and only measurable once the ring exists, so it stays as roadmap M3 rather than contaminating this round's falsifier. Cache-line padding at 128 bytes and the codegen flags are folded in because they are the same edit at near-zero risk on this host.

### Hypothesis
The baseline spends nearly all per-operation time on work that the SPSC workload does not require: `Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>` in `src/lib.rs` costs one lock acquire/release, one `malloc`, and one `free` per item, plus a pointer dereference to reach the payload. Replacing it with a lock-free ring — two 128-byte-separated atomic indices over one preallocated slot slab, each side caching the peer index so the fast path never loads the peer's cache line — removes all three costs and leaves only an 8-byte copy plus one release store per operation, raising `total_ops_per_sec` by an order of magnitude.

### Activation evidence
1) `otool -tV queue-candidate.so` for `_vsq_try_enqueue` and `_vsq_try_dequeue` shows no `bl` to `_pthread_mutex_lock`, `_malloc`, or `_free` on the success path. 2) `nm -gU queue-candidate.so` still lists all nine `vsq_*` symbols. 3) A local 1P/1C free-running harness (implementer-written, not the canonical benchmark) at capacity 1024 / value size 8 reports successful-op rate for the new build and for the committed baseline build, and the new build is at least 10x the baseline. Report all three, plus the raw local numbers.

### Falsification criteria
Activation is confirmed (no lock/alloc calls on the hot path, exports intact) but the local 1P/1C harness shows under 2x the baseline successful-op rate. That would mean per-operation synchronization and allocation are not the binding cost and that cross-core coherence latency on the shared index lines already dominated the baseline, so this mechanism cannot carry the metric on this host. Also falsifying: the ring passes locally but the trusted correctness gate reports a linearizability, conservation, or ABI-status failure that is inherent to the design rather than to a fixable coding slip.

### Expected effect (forecast)
Baseline per item pair is roughly one uncontended-to-contended mutex round trip plus a malloc/free pair, order 100-250 ns; the ring's per item pair is an 8-byte copy, two release stores, and an amortized peer-index reload, order 5-25 ns. Forecast 10-40x on `total_ops_per_sec`. The upper end is unlikely to be reached because the score counts only successful operations and the consumer's per-success work in the trusted runner (payload validation plus two fingerprint mixes) becomes the new rate limit, so the realistic landing zone is 10-25x.

### Minimum acceptance criteria
Retain only if the trusted median `total_ops_per_sec` is at least 3x the baseline median with the correctness gate passing and no tradeoff axis configured (`pareto-frontier.md` records no objective axes, so throughput is the sole retention axis). The 3x floor sits far below the 10-40x forecast on purpose: the benchmark takes the median of three 10-second repetitions, so run-to-run noise is expected in the low single-digit percent, and a 3x result is unambiguously outside it while still leaving room for the consumer-side rate limit to cap the gain well short of the forecast. Below 3x with activation confirmed, treat the mechanism as underperforming and park it rather than retaining an unexplained partial win. Accept no correctness regression and no increase in resident memory beyond the slab itself.

### Invariants
Authoritative and unchanged: the ABI in `include/vibesys_queue_abi.h` and the lifecycle, ownership, and semantic rules in `CANDIDATE_CONTRACT.md` (both inside the resolved `vibesys-evaluator-queue` package; the local mirror of the exported surface is `src/ffi.rs`). Do not change exported symbol names, signatures, or `ABI_VERSION`. The build contract in `Makefile` — `cargo build --release --locked` producing `./queue-candidate.so` — must keep working unchanged.

Hypothesis-specific constraints, all derived from the contract and the evaluator source:

- Operations are try-style. `vsq_try_enqueue` and `vsq_try_dequeue` must never block, sleep, or loop waiting for the peer.
- `VSQ_FULL` may be returned only when the queue is genuinely at capacity, and `VSQ_EMPTY` only when it is genuinely empty, both judged at a point inside the call. A cached peer index may drive the fast path, but before returning FULL or EMPTY the code must re-load the peer's atomic index and re-check. Publishing the consumer's head lazily or in batches is forbidden: it would make FULL legal while the abstract queue has room.
- `VSQ_EMPTY` and `VSQ_INVALID` from dequeue must leave both the output buffer and `*output_length` untouched, and must leave the value queued. Read the stored length and compare it against `output_capacity` before copying any bytes.
- Never write more than `output_capacity` bytes. Never retain the caller's input or output pointer past the call.
- For valid arguments, only OK/FULL and OK/EMPTY are acceptable; any `VSQ_INVALID` or `VSQ_INTERNAL_ERROR` on a valid call fails evaluation. Keep the existing rejection of out-of-range producer/consumer ids.
- The crate is `panic = "abort"`: a panic kills the trusted runner. Slab allocation must be fallible and return `STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR` on failure, and the hot path must not use anything that can panic (no bounds-checked indexing on the hot path, no unwrap).
- Correctness must hold for non-power-of-two capacities. The gate runs capacities 1024, 1, 2, and 3, and ABI profiles (1024, 8), (7, 257), (3, 1 MiB). Whatever wrap scheme is chosen must be exercised at those shapes. Actual value lengths 0, 1, 7, 8, 9, intermediate, and maximum are all probed, so length must be stored per slot, not assumed constant.
- Host is Apple M4 arm64: `hw.cachelinesize` is 128, so shared-index padding is 128 bytes, not 64. L1D is 64 KiB, so keep the 1024-slot benchmark slab well inside it.

### Task
Replace the queue core in `src/lib.rs` with a lock-free SPSC ring. `src/ffi.rs` should need no signature changes; keep it as the thin ABI shim and mark the shim plus the core operations `#[inline]`.

Component and interface:

- `QueueState` owns one fallibly-allocated slab of `slots` fixed-stride slots plus two shared indices. Each slot holds its own length header and its payload contiguously (for example a `u64` length followed by `max_value_size` payload bytes, stride rounded up for alignment) so one operation touches one cache line at value size 8. A parallel length array is the weaker alternative because it doubles the lines touched per operation.
- Producer index `tail` and consumer index `head` are monotonic `AtomicU64` counters, each alone on its own 128-byte-aligned, 128-byte-padded region so neither side's store invalidates the other's line. Monotonic counters make full and empty unambiguous without a spare slot.
- Suggested wrap scheme, since capacity 3 and 7 must work and a `%` on the hot path is a division: allocate `slots = next_power_of_two(capacity)` and index with a mask, while enforcing the logical bound with `tail - head == capacity`. Over-allocation is at most 2x, and the gate's worst case (capacity 3, 1 MiB values) is 4 slots and 4 MiB. Any equivalent division-free scheme is fine; state which you chose.
- `Producer` and `Consumer` handles carry their own private cached copy of the peer index. Enqueue fast path: compare `tail` against the cached `head`; only when it reports full, acquire-load the real `head` into the cache and re-check; return `VSQ_FULL` only if it is still full. Dequeue is the mirror image against `tail`. Handles are per-thread by contract, so this private state needs no synchronization, but pad/align the handle allocations so two handles cannot share a line.
- Ordering: write the length header and payload, then `Release`-store the advanced `tail`. Consumer `Acquire`-loads `tail`, reads header and payload, then `Release`-stores the advanced `head`. Each side loads its own index `Relaxed`.
- Add a small-length fast path in both directions: at length 8 do a single unaligned `u64` copy instead of calling `memcpy`, falling back to `copy_nonoverlapping` otherwise. At value size 8 this removes a libc call from every operation.
- In `Cargo.toml`, add `lto = "fat"`, `codegen-units = 1`, and `opt-level = 3` to `[profile.release]`, keeping `panic = "abort"`. Do not touch `Cargo.lock`; profile changes do not invalidate `--locked`.
- Keep the existing `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests passing and extend them to cover capacity 1, capacity 3, zero-length values, maximum-length values, undersized-output retry, and wraparound across more than `capacity` items.

Staged evaluation, cheapest first, stopping as soon as a stage fails:

1. `cargo test --release` for the extended unit tests, and `make` to confirm `./queue-candidate.so` is produced.
2. Activation checks as listed in the activation evidence field: the `otool` disassembly check, `nm -gU`, and the local 1P/1C harness comparing the new build against the committed baseline build.
3. Only if 1 and 2 pass, hand off. Do not re-run the framework's canonical benchmark; it runs after review.

Verification strategy — the minimum that exercises the failure-prone paths, which here are the wrap arithmetic, the FULL/EMPTY boundary, and the ordering:

- Single-threaded boundary test at capacity 1, 2, 3, and 7: fill to exactly capacity, assert the next enqueue is FULL, drain to empty, assert the next dequeue is EMPTY, and repeat across at least three wraps so the mask/wrap path is exercised past the slab end.
- Mixed-length test at max_value_size 257 and at 1 MiB with capacity 3: enqueue lengths 0, 1, 7, 8, 9, and max, dequeue them, and assert both bytes and returned lengths match FIFO order.
- Undersized-output test: enqueue a value, dequeue into a buffer one byte too small, assert `VSQ_INVALID`, assert the output buffer and the length out-parameter are byte-for-byte unchanged, then dequeue into an adequate buffer and assert the value is intact.
- Two-thread stress in the local harness: run producer and consumer for a few seconds at capacity 1024 with a per-item sequence number, assert every dequeued value is the next expected sequence number with no gaps and no repeats, and assert enqueued minus dequeued equals what the final drain returns. This is the cheapest check that would catch a missing Acquire or Release.
- Run the two-thread stress under a debug build too; the release build can hide an ordering bug behind timing.

If any stage fails, isolate along the changed dataflow — slot addressing, then length handling, then index ordering — before rebuilding and re-measuring; do not fix only the leaf assertion that tripped.

### Pass criteria
1. Activation: the `otool -tV` disassembly of `_vsq_try_enqueue` and `_vsq_try_dequeue` shows no branch to `_pthread_mutex_lock`, `_malloc`, or `_free`; `nm -gU queue-candidate.so` lists all nine `vsq_*` symbols; the local 1P/1C harness reports at least 10x the committed baseline's successful-op rate. Raw numbers reported, not just a verdict.
2. Correctness: `cargo test --release` and `cargo test` (debug) both pass, including the extended capacity-1/2/3/7, zero-length, max-length, undersized-output, and multi-wrap cases, plus the two-thread sequence-conservation stress in both profiles.
3. Contract: no exported symbol name or signature changed, `ABI_VERSION` still 1, no blocking, sleeping, or retry loop anywhere in enqueue or dequeue, FULL and EMPTY each preceded by a fresh atomic re-load of the peer index, dequeue leaving output and `*output_length` untouched on EMPTY and INVALID, and no panicking construct on the hot path.
4. Build: `make` succeeds from clean via `cargo build --release --locked`, `Cargo.lock` unmodified, `./queue-candidate.so` present.
5. Cleanup: no leftover scratch binaries, profiling shims, debug printing, or dead mutex/VecDeque code; the local harness, if committed, lives outside the hot library path and does not affect the cdylib build.
6. Evidence: report the local before/after ops-per-second numbers, the chosen wrap scheme, the slot layout and stride, and the padding size actually used.

# Queue Candidate Contract v1

This document is the normative interface between the evaluator and an untrusted
queue implementation. Candidate behavior is accepted only when it satisfies
this contract; evaluator implementation details are described separately in
[`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md).

## Required artifact

Candidates must provide a shared library named `queue-candidate.so` in the
workspace root. The library may be implemented in any language or combination
of languages that exports the C ABI declared in
`include/vibesys_queue_abi.h`.

The queue uses VibeSys's `inprocess` execution mode: the evaluator loads and
invokes the library directly inside an evaluator-owned Rust process. The

semantic, and error requirements.

correctness checks it runs in a worker process controlled by the Go Porcupine
checker. During performance measurement it calls the same ABI directly from
native producer and consumer threads.

producer and consumer counts for the scenario. Queue capacity is measured in
items, not bytes.

The runner creates one opaque producer handle per producer and one opaque
consumer handle per consumer before timing begins. Each handle is used by
exactly one native thread, while different handles are called concurrently
against the same queue. An implementation that does not need per-thread state
may use thin handles that only reference the queue.

The runner destroys all producer and consumer handles before destroying the
queue. It drains the queue before normal destruction.

## Operations and ownership

`vsq_try_enqueue` receives a byte pointer and length:

- `VSQ_OK` means the value was copied into the queue.
- `VSQ_FULL` means all item capacity was occupied or reserved and the call
  retained nothing.
- The input pointer is valid only for the duration of the call. The candidate
  must not retain or access it after returning.
- Length must not exceed the configured maximum value size.

`vsq_try_dequeue` receives caller-owned output storage:

- `VSQ_OK` means the complete oldest value was copied to `output` and
  `output_length` was set.
- `VSQ_EMPTY` means no published item was available. Output storage and
  `output_length` must remain unchanged.
- `VSQ_INVALID` means the output is null or too small for the oldest value. The
  value remains queued, and output storage and `output_length` remain unchanged.
- The candidate must not retain the output pointer after returning.
- A candidate must never write more than `output_capacity` bytes.

For valid enqueue inputs, only `VSQ_OK` and `VSQ_FULL` are normal results. For a
sufficient dequeue output, only `VSQ_OK` and `VSQ_EMPTY` are normal results.
`VSQ_INTERNAL_ERROR`, or `VSQ_INVALID` for otherwise valid arguments, fails
evaluation.

Operations are try-style: they do not wait for space to become free or for an
item to arrive. Successful operations preserve one global FIFO order and every
successfully enqueued item is returned exactly once.

SPSC and MPSC use an exact linearizable bounded-queue model. A successful
enqueue atomically appends an item, `VSQ_FULL` is legal only when the abstract
queue is at capacity, a successful dequeue atomically removes the oldest item,
and `VSQ_EMPTY` is legal only when the abstract queue is empty.

MPMC uses a reservation-aware bounded-queue model to match queues that acquire
capacity before copying and publishing an item. A successful enqueue has two
ordered internal events within its call interval:

1. reservation consumes one item of capacity;
2. publication makes the copied item visible at the FIFO tail.

`VSQ_FULL` is legal when published items plus unpublished reservations equal
capacity. `VSQ_EMPTY` is legal when no item has been published, even if an
enqueue currently holds a reservation. Consequently, a capacity-one MPMC
history may contain an in-flight enqueue that later returns `VSQ_OK`, an
overlapping enqueue that returns `VSQ_FULL`, and an intervening dequeue that
returns `VSQ_EMPTY`. Publication order defines the global FIFO order. Both
reservation and publication must occur within the successful enqueue call, so
a completed enqueue is visible to every later non-overlapping dequeue.

The evaluator selects a fixed `--value-size` for each run, currently bounded to
8 bytes through 1 MiB. Every measured value in a run has that size. Candidate
implementations must still honor any operation length up to the maximum passed
to `vsq_queue_create`.

The producer may overwrite its input immediately after enqueue returns, and
the consumer may overwrite its output immediately after dequeue returns. This
deliberately requires copying and makes allocation and byte movement part of
the measured implementation.

The correctness gate probes actual lengths 0, 1, 7, 8, 9, intermediate, and
maximum for 8-byte, 257-byte, and 1 MiB queue profiles. It also checks input
retention, undersized-output retry, concurrent short/full-buffer consumers, and
unchanged output on empty and invalid dequeues before running concurrent
Porcupine histories. Each history is decided under a time budget, and a history
the checker cannot decide within it fails the gate exactly as a violation does.

The evaluator may run multiple independent benchmark repetitions. The reported
`total_ops_per_sec` is the median repetition; the detailed JSON report also
lists the individual `total_ops_per_sec_samples` values.

## Unsupported contracts

Version 1 does not support zero-copy ownership transfer, queue-managed producer
buffers, batched operations, or lossy queue semantics. A candidate must not
infer such behavior from implementation details. Any future contract with those
semantics requires a new version.

## Trust boundary

The Go correctness checker remains in a separate process from candidate native
code and owns expected payloads, call/return timestamps, histories, and the
Porcupine verdict. The measured Rust benchmark and candidate library share an
address space to avoid per-operation IPC and FFI transitions. Consequently,
performance scoring assumes cooperative native candidate code; Rust memory
safety does not isolate the runner from a hostile library.

For scored execution, the Go and Rust evaluators, this contract, and the ABI
header come from a trusted input snapshot.

#define VSQ_ABI_VERSION 1u

typedef struct vsq_queue vsq_queue;
typedef struct vsq_producer vsq_producer;
typedef struct vsq_consumer vsq_consumer;

#define VSQ_INVALID 3u

extern "C" {
#endif

    uint64_t max_value_size,

    uint32_t consumer_count,
    vsq_queue **queue_out);

void vsq_queue_destroy(vsq_queue *queue);

vsq_status vsq_producer_create(

    uint32_t producer_id,

}

The source is organized as follows:

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `*.go` | CLI, candidate process control, histories, Porcupine checking, benchmark aggregation, evaluator result stream |
| `native_runner/src/abi.rs` | Dynamic loading and typed ownership of the candidate C ABI |
| `native_runner/src/protocol.rs` | Correctness worker and per-lane socket protocol |
| `native_runner/src/probe.rs` | ABI edge-case and copying-lifetime probes |
| `native_runner/src/benchmark.rs` | Native timed producer and consumer threads |
| `include/vibesys_queue_abi.h` | Candidate ABI declarations |
| `examples/data-structures/repositories/queue-rs` | Local repository-shaped untrusted Rust candidate |

Go owns the correctness model because Porcupine is a mature Go implementation.
Rust owns all candidate FFI so C ABI loading, native handle lifetimes, and direct
benchmark calls are implemented once. The candidate never interacts directly
with Go.

VibeSys copies this package to `_evaluator/<name>` in the candidate workspace
before running it, so it must build from a relocated tree with no path back to
this repository. Every Go dependency, including the evaluator SDK
(`github.com/uw-syfi/vibesys/sdk/vs-evaluator/vseval`), is an ordinary published
module requirement resolved from the module proxy: no relative `replace`, no
committed `vendor/`. To change the SDK and this evaluator together, use a
developer-local Go workspace, described in [sdk/README.md](../../../sdk/README.md).
